parts.note: reads like an exam sheet a pupil sits, but is the indicator paper used in the lab to test acid or alkali

explanation.surface: A science pupil hands in an examination paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'test paper' sounds like an exam; it is the paper strip that turns red in acid and blue in alkali.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus is the dyed strip a chemist dips into a solution to tell acid from alkali.

parts.note: uplift sounds like inspiring someone, but here it is raising a body into the air by supernatural power, as at a seance

explanation.surface: A sermon meant to raise the congregation's spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise or float in the air by occult or spiritual means is the medium's trick of the seance room.

definitions.meaning: to debate or talk something through with others
read literally, the talk is over once the lecture ends

explanation.surface: Questions about when discussion can start after a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk a matter through is to discuss it; and when a lecture ends, the talk is literally done.

clue.text: As far as one is able

definitions.meaning: as far as, reaching a limit
capable of, as in 'not feeling ... the job'

explanation.surface: Someone doing the best within their own limits.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase marks a limit ('until', 'as far as') and also means capable, as in being equal to a task.

clue.text: Ready money affected by the Shops Act

indicators.note: something affected is altered, so the letters of the act's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cash in hand changed under new trading laws for shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected by' signals rearranging the letters of SHOPS ACT. The Shops Act was British legislation governing shop opening hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash paid immediately on delivery is ready money, money available on the spot.

clue.text: Oscar's tiptop variety of bar snack

indicators.note: a variety is a different arrangement, so the letters of the two words are reworked

parts.note: the possessive's S is kept as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A man named Oscar has a first-rate choice of pub nibbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' shuffles OSCARS and TIPTOP together. The S of 'Oscar's' counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin fried slices of tuber sold in packets are the classic pub nibble.

parts.note: Don Quixote famously charged at windmills with his lance, a joust-style attack

explanation.surface: An idealistic but hopeless attack.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Quixote's famous charge was at windmills, which he took for giants; the jousting word for such a charge is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge with a lance as in a joust is the act Quixote made famous against windmills.

definitions.meaning: combat, as soldiers seeing battle
a legal proceeding brought in court

explanation.surface: Combat in the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers see combat when in battle; a case brought in court is also a legal proceeding of this name.

clue.text: Problem has bearing on the French

parts.note: taken as written
a compass bearing such as south, S
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Something troubling bears on the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' is a compass point; here S for south.
explanation.definitionFit: A bother or annoying difficulty is a problem.

clue.text: Farewell, thank you for the dance

parts.note: vale is Latin for goodbye
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye and thanks after a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: VALE is Latin for farewell; TA is British slang for thank you. 'for the' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A valeta is an old-time ballroom round dance in triple time.

clue.text: Runners allowed to enter various heats

indicators.note: one piece goes into the middle of the other
various forms suggests the letters are scrambled

parts.note: allowed means let

explanation.surface: Competitors permitted to take part in several qualifying races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heats' looks like part of the race scene but is anagram fodder signalled by 'various'; 'to enter' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprinters and distance racers are track competitors.

clue.text: Describing a coast-to coast athletic event in Malta?

definitions.text: Describing a coast-to coast athletic event in Malta?

parts.words: Describing a coast-to coast athletic event in Malta?
parts.note: a race across open land; Malta was awarded the George Cross, so it is the island known for that medal

explanation.surface: A race from one shore of Malta to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: Malta was awarded the George Cross in 1942, making it the 'cross' nation; a race over open ground carries the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-distance running race over fields and open terrain bears this name; Malta, holder of the George Cross, is wittily such a nation.

clue.text: The correct pace for young Copperfield

definitions.meaning: a horse's steady gait between walk and canter
in Dickens's David Copperfield, Aunt Betsey calls the boy by this pet name

explanation.surface: Teaching a young lad the right walking speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's jogging gait shares its name with Betsey Trotwood's nickname for David in Dickens's novel.

indicators.note: in an unusual order, so the letters of great are shuffled

explanation.surface: Praise for a film star's remarkable performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' signals rearranging GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish film star Garbo's first name.

definitions.meaning: the hood on a monk's habit
a hooded cap on a chimney stops it smoking by blocking downdraughts

explanation.surface: A remedy for giving up cigarettes involving a monk's hood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkshood' also names a poisonous plant, a false trail; here it is a monk's hood. A chimney with a hooded cap smokes less.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar's hood and the hooded chimney cap that stops a fire smoking share this name.

clue.text: Tinned beef in this form will poison you

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: tinned food comes in a tin
beef comes from an ox

explanation.surface: A warning that canned meat can make you ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinned beef' is read literally: the beef word sealed inside the can word, with 'in' as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisonous substance produced by living things, as in spoiled food, is a toxin.

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Seeing a notice on the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is a noun, a proverb, not the past of see.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb.

indicators.note: dashed suggests broken up, so the letters of the three words are scrambled

explanation.surface: An excited cry as signals of dots and dashes arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashed' rearranges HERE COME DOTS; the whole clue also describes the signalling code of dots and dashes.
explanation.definitionFit: The telegraph code spells letters in dots and dashes.

definitions.meaning: bears comparison with, equals
equals or corresponds to

explanation.surface: Lighting a candle using matches.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear comparison with something or equal it; matches in the sense of equals.

definitions.meaning: to hold out against a deal
to stick out, protrude

explanation.surface: Declining to sign up to a proposed scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold out against agreement, and to protrude or be conspicuous.

parts.note: getting hitched means marrying, so a place where cowboys tie up their horses is jokingly a wedding venue

explanation.surface: Cowboys getting married at a register office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hitched' means married; a cowboy hitches his horse to a post.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail or post where riders tether horses; 'hitch' also means to wed.

clue.text: Add salt and pepper as one's cooking

indicators.note: cooking means mixing or altering, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive's S counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: Seasoning food while it is being cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges AS ONES, with the S of 'one's' counted.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding condiments to food to flavour it is what this verb means.

clue.text: Bill to boast about Polish city

parts.note: to crow is to boast
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Bragging about a restaurant bill in a Polish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal and 'to' a link. The bill is an account, abbreviated in crosswords to its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracow (Krakow) is a historic city in southern Poland.

parts.note: sound seems to mean valid or reliable, but is noise, which hearing organs take in

explanation.surface: People who believe only reliable arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning valid; it is noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The organs of hearing take in noise.

definitions.meaning: discards or throws away
low spirits, as in being down in the ...

explanation.surface: Someone shaking off low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard is to dump; low spirits are 'the dumps'.

definitions.meaning: brand new, as in spick-and-... or ...-new
a matched team harnessed together

explanation.surface: A new team of horses brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: A team of matched horses is a span; and 'span-new' means brand new.

definitions.meaning: take care of, as in babysitting
to dislike or be against

explanation.surface: Tending a particular thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To take care of something; and to object, as in 'I don't mind'.

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Struggling with a difficulty, darling?
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is nil in tennis, the letter O. 'with' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese heavyweight wrestling is this sport.

parts.note: investments read as in-vestments, the holy vestments kept in a church's side room

explanation.surface: A place for sound financial investing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investments' hides 'vestments', the robes a priest keeps in this church room.
explanation.definitionFit: The church room where vestments and sacred vessels are stored.

clue.text: Size of a book or volume on love

indicators.note: on means placed after, here alongside

parts.note: a quart is a volume measure
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Measuring a romance novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' looks like a book; here it is a liquid measure. 'or' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A book format where each sheet is folded twice to make four leaves.

clue.text: Unfortunately, Don's away at the moment

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the possessive's S counts as a letter

explanation.surface: Bad news: Don is currently absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges DONS AWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: These days, presently.

parts.note: stays seems a verb, but stays are the stiff bones of a laced undergarment that supports the figure

explanation.surface: Someone who remains to support a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' reads as remains; it is the old name for a boned undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight boned undergarment shaping the torso, once called stays.
